headline: Analysts say US shipments of Nvidia's advanced AI chips to the UAE and Saudi Arabia are running late because of investment talks, security conditions and fears the technology could leak to China.
score_reason: Kept at pool score: an analysis from this week with named experts, but it explains a delay rather than reporting a new decision.
importance_line: It affects Gulf AI developers waiting for hardware, US officials weighing security against sales, and Nvidia, but the reasons come from analysts and no government comment is reported.
summary: Arabian Gulf Business Insight (AGBI) reports that the US Commerce Department approved 35,000 Nvidia Blackwell chips a year ago for the AI developers G42 in the UAE and Humain in Saudi Arabia, and that both have received only part of them. Nazak Nikakhtar, a trade and national security partner at the law firm Wiley Rein who held senior roles in the first Trump administration, said she thinks Commerce is still waiting on Gulf investment pledges that have only partly materialised, and Ruth Berry, who leads Nvidia's global policy, said slow deliveries could boost the appeal of Chinese offerings.
